thread:
Marc: Heads up — noticed a weird burn spike for the eu-west-1 SLO around 09:12 UTC even though token/sec is down. anyone else seeing this?
Anya: Huh, saw a blip on the regional dashboard earlier. Was going to ask if sampling changed on exporters. :thinking_face:
Marc: Here's the panel query I used (grafana, per-region rollup):
```
sum by(region) (increase(gpu_saturation_seconds_total{region=~"eu-.*"}[5m])) / sum by(region) (increase(requests_total{region=~"eu-.*"}[5m]))
```
Leah: That query mixes two ergonomically different counters — gpu_saturation_seconds_total is a histogram-like counter from the runtime, requests_total is app-level. Might amplify noise when request rate drops.
Tim: Can you paste the raw timeseries? want to see if a single shard is noisy.
Marc: Pasted small sample below — eu-west-1 jumps at 09:12 then decays by 09:18: 
```
eu-west-1: saturation_rate 0.04 -> 0.32 -> 0.06 (5m buckets)
node-exporter scrape time: 09:11:30, 09:16:30, 09:21:30
```
Anya: I also checked alert history — alert `SLO:gpu-saturation:high` fired at 09:13 and again at 09:14 (flap). Looks like burncount calc is 1m resolution then summed to 5m, so one high sample creates a big burn.
Leah: Propose we change the SLI definition: currently it's using instantaneous GPU saturation aggregated across shards (`avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[1m]) > 0.9`) which is sensitive. Suggest moving to `max_over_time` at per-node then p95 across nodes, and smooth with `avg_over_time(...[5m])` to reduce single-sample noise.
Tim: Agreed. Also want to check if any scrape/config changes happened — @sre-bot can you surface monitoring config deploys around 09:00-09:20?
sre-bot: deploy-log: monitoring/prometheus-exporter config updated by deploy-bot at 2025-11-12T09:05:12Z — PR #5423 (reduce metric cardinality). Commit: 9f3a2c4
deploy-bot: deploy:monitoring succeeded: apply monitoring/prometheus-exporter (revision 9f3a2c4) — finished 09:07:01Z
Anya: That PR removed a low-cardinality label and changed scrape_interval for some exporter jobs from 15s -> 60s in eu-west-1 for cost reasons. That explains coarser sampling. :grimacing:
Leah: Bingo. So lower scrape frequency + one noisy sample -> exaggerated burn. Two things: revert eu-west scrape bump for GPU exporters OR adjust SLO calc to be robust to 60s scrapes.
Marc: Revert would cost $$$, but we can tighten the SLO math. Suggested PromQL change (draft):
```
// per-node saturation smoothed over 5m, then p95 across nodes
quantile_over_time(0.95, avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization{region="eu-west-1"}[5m]))
```
Tim: I like that. Also suggest switching error budget accounting to use 5m windows (instead of 1m) for burnrate to reduce flap. This preserves meaningful incidents but reduces noise.
Anya: We should also add a synthetic SLI (end-to-end tail latency) so we don't rely solely on infra counters. If GPU saturation metric is noisy, we still catch user impact.
Leah: Agreed. I'll sketch a runbook change: - change alert threshold to p95>0.85 over 5m - burn calculation use 5m windows - create synthetic-sli job (small traffic to /health/gpu-check with labeled tenant) - note monitoring deploy PR rollback only if necessary.
Marc: Can you open the alert PR and tag me? I'll put rough SLA impact calc (cost vs errorbudget risk). :+1:
Tim: I'll take the alert PR. Will add tests and update grafana panels to show both old and new SLI side-by-side.
Anya: Also adding a Grafana variable `scrape_interval` to panel so we can eyeball correlation across regions easily.
Leah: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation (draft) — adding steps to validate exporters, check commits, and query examples.
Marc: Plan sounds good. TL;DR: root cause = scrape_interval change + sensitive SLI math. Fix = smoothing + p95 + synthetic SLI. Action items: @Tim open PR, @Leah update runbook, @Anya audit other regions for similar changes. :eyes:
Tim: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/monitoring/pull/5480 — small change to alert rule and burn calc. marking for review.
Leah: I'll review once CI passes. If we still see big burns after smoothing, we revert the eu-west scrape change.
Marc: Thanks all. will follow up in SLO sync later. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Tim: thumbs up :thumbsup:
